title: Shoutout to all the Fringe-style shows I’ve seen over the years that ...
transcript: I posted a video with the longest theatre productions I've ever seen by runtime and now I'm gonna do my top 5 shortest! Two quick notes before I start: same as my longest runtimes video I'm going by runtime-per-ticket so if I buy a ticket to an evening of 10-minute plays performed back to back they don't count individually, only as a group And for the purposes of this list, I decided to exclude any of these interactive theatrical experiences that don't use live performers. In 5th place, Prometheus Firebringer this was a performance art piece at Theatre for a New Audience a couple years ago that compared Eyyy-aye to the Prometheus myth. there was a lot more to it than that but in any case it ran a brief 46 minutes! in 4th place, just this past January a site specific production of Eugene O'Neill's nautical thriller In the Zone, performed on an antique ship and it was a breezy 42 minutes in third place The Democracy Project another site-specific play this one performed in New York's Federal Hall and the performance I attended clocked in at a mere 39 minutes before I get to my top two go ahead and tell me in the comments what is the shortest runtime of a ticketed performance you've ever seen in theatre? In 2nd place, the Gummy Bears’ Great War about gummy bears going to war with dinosaurs it was the shortest production with live actors that I saw at the Edinburgh Fringe at only 30 minutes but in first place is a performance that Bill Irwin did outdoors in 2020 called The Busking Project and even though it was kind of an homage to impromptu street performance and technically anyone passing by could watch it it was still a ticketed event with a specific start time there was an audience viewing area where I had an assigned spot and at a mere 9 minutes long it's definitely the shortest overall theatre performance I've ever seen
